all claim fields within their encoded widths (u32/u64/u128, 32-byte hashes, chain id 1..64 printable ASCII)
(n-1)*223182562500 < gas_limit: no receipt is pushed to the delayed queue
every receipt is Receipt::V0 / ReceiptEnum::Action with exactly one Transfer action and no input/output data dependencies

the revealed partial-trie bytes are <= 3,000,000 (storage-proof soft limit never reached)
each receiver Account exists when its receipt is applied and is a 72-byte AccountV1
after the credit, amount'+locked >= 10^19*storage_usage or storage_usage <= 770
G*min(gas_price, block_gas_price), G*(gas_price-min) and the total tokens burnt fit in u128
the chunk applies only these incoming receipts: no transactions, no local/delayed/yield receipts, no validator-account update, new chunk

rationale.note: N_v = 50 chunk validators PER SHARD (governance decision, 2026-10-06). The per-chunk statement is one shard's chunk at one height; it is verified by that shard's chunk-validator committee, so N_v counts one shard's validators, not all validators. 50 is the governed committee size; the v1 draft's mainnet observation (epoch 4835, 2026-10-05: 415 validators, 10 shards, 84.0-84.1 distinct endorsers per shard per height; 105 mandate seats per shard) is kept as context and as a sensitivity column, not as the price. Only the verify and bandwidth terms scale with N_v, and both scale linearly, so N_v moves the prover:validator balance but not the ranking among candidates whose cost is all validator-side. FUTURE (not priced here, docs/BENCHMARK_SPEC.md 14.11): a whole-block statement covering S shards is verified by every validator, N_v = 50 x S, against a re-execution baseline that grows with S. Re-check per season.
sources: governance decision 2026-10-06 (BENCHMARK_SPEC 14.10, decision 1: N_v = 50 validators per shard)

rationale.note: Reference validator profile: NEAR's published chunk-validator spec is 'x86_64 with at least 8 physical cores' (recommended and minimal). The judge measures verify pinned to the first 8 benchmark CPUs; on the live host those are CPUs 0-7 (CCD0, 8 physical cores, SMT siblings 16-23 idle), i.e. the reference profile; the references of the v1-6 and v3 D0 challenges were re-measured there on 2026-10-06 with the verify drift control (BENCHMARK_SPEC 14.4: v3 D0 confirmed; v1-6 batch-16 not reproducible within 30 000 ppm). Charging allocated vCPUs x wall time (not guest CPU time) keeps the only trusted clock (supervisor wall) and makes parallel verifiers cost what they reserve.

c_cpu = 7.61e-6 USD per vCPU-second = USD 160/month for 8 vCPU (AWS m5a.2xlarge, CPU part, the first cost estimate NEAR publishes for a chunk validator): 160 / (730 h x 8 x 3600 s). The same price is used for the prover (chunk producer) because both run on the same class of node. ESTIMATE: on-demand cloud list price; bare metal is cheaper, reserved instances ~40% cheaper. Only ratios to the baseline enter the score, so a uniform CPU price change does not move CPU-only comparisons; it moves the CPU:bandwidth balance.

c_bw = per-validator network cost of one proof byte = egress price x upload amplification. Upload amplification from nearcore partial-witness distribution: Reed-Solomon with WITNESS_RATIO_DATA_PARTS = 0.6 and one part per chunk validator; each validator forwards its part to the other N-2 validators, so it uploads (N-2)/floor(0.6 N) x the proof: 1.64 at N = 84 (v1 draft), 1.60 at N = 50 (48/30); ingress is free on clouds. Egress price ESTIMATE USD 0.05/GB (AWS >150 TB/month tier; first tier is 0.09; unmetered bare metal is lower). Governed value: 8.2e-11 USD/B = 82000 fUSD/B, the v1 draft constant retained by governance decision (2026-10-06); the N = 50 derivation gives 8.0e-11 (-2.4%), well inside the egress-price uncertainty. Not modelled: the chunk producer's own ~1.7 x upload (one node, ~2-3% of the N_v term), compression (candidates may compress; decompression is inside verify time).
